The average number of CHIP variants per sample, after excluding intronic, intergenic, and UTR variants (and dropping reference genotypes), is **52.3 variants per sample** (mean = 52.291; median 52; range 39–66 across the 86 samples).

Method (executed end-to-end, `inspect_analysis.py`):
- Parsed all 86 workbooks (33-column two-level header, identical structure; 57,258 rows total; 0 malformed).
- Dropped reference calls: Zygosity `Reference` (44,211) and empty/NaN (1,151) — non-variant genotypes, not CHIP carriers.
- Kept variant zygosities (`Heterozygous` 7,303 + `Homozygous Variant` 4,593 = 11,896 rows) and kept coding/splice SO classes: synonymous_variant, missense_variant, splice_region_variant, inframe_insertion, inframe_deletion, frameshift_variant.
- Excluded intronic/intergenic/UTR/non-coding SO classes: intron_variant, 3_prime_UTR_variant, 5_prime_UTR_variant, 5_prime_UTR_premature_start_codon_gain_variant, upstream_gene_variant (and intergenic_* — none present in this exome data); 7,399 variant rows were removed by this annotation filter.
- Count = rows per sample == distinct (Chr:Pos, Ref/Alt) sites (0 intra-sample duplicates after filtering), averaged over all 86 samples (every sample had ≥1 counted variant; no zero-count samples).

Applied assumptions: (1) Reference/empty-zygosity rows are dropped because they are reference genotypes, not variant carriers (keeping them would inflate the mean to ~300, which is clearly wrong); (2) splice_region_variant is retained as a coding-affecting class — as a footnote, excluding it too would give 47.2; (3) exact-string matching on the SO column, valid because every row is single-term; (4) upstream_gene_variant is treated as non-coding and excluded (+0.03 if kept); (5) denominator = 86 samples (unambiguous since all samples have ≥1 variant); (6) DP≥10/GQ≥20/PASS filters already applied by the data folder, confirmed `Filter`='PASS' on all rows.
